After a write, replicas may briefly return older values until updates propagate. Clients should tolerate this delay rather than assume every reader is immediately synchronized.
Serializable transactions prevent certain conflicting concurrent outcomes. They are not a promise about asynchronous replica propagation.
Records provide concise immutable data carriers. Mutable objects inside a record still require careful ownership.
An ETag identifies a representation. A stale If-Match must fail rather than overwrite newer content.
Revise binary search, graph traversal and heap operations before the practice interview.
DNS resolves names to records. It does not encrypt application traffic.
TCP retransmits lost segments and preserves byte ordering. Applications still need message framing.
A worker may submit twice after losing an acknowledgement. Use idempotency where possible; do not claim exactly-once external delivery.
